title: Platform Seller Elevator Arsenal (draft)
content:
Slide 1 — One-line purpose:
Platform Seller Elevator Arsenal — a stripped-down, repeatable toolkit to close a pilot in a single buyer conversation and a 90-minute tech touch. Keep it under 3 minutes; use these lines.

Slide 2 — Who this is for (persona):
- Platform/Integrations sellers pitching platform teams, integration architects, and infra leads.
- Typical buying trigger: performance unpredictability, cost spikes, or noisy latency SLAs from existing LLM endpoints.
- Decision factors: latency SLOs, predictable unit economics, private deployment needs, and integration effort.

Slide 3 — Opening 30s script (quick hook):
- "We help platform teams get predictable LLM inference at scale — <10% lower per-token cost on common prompts and consistent p95 latency under Xms without refactoring your app."
- If asked for proof: "We have a 90-minute pilot runbook and a sample dashboard you can spin up with your sample prompt set."

Slide 4 — Three-minute demo flow (what to show live):
1) Quick architecture slide (30s): route + model catalog + fallback tiers.
2) Latency & cost dashboard (45s): token-level spotlight, p50/p95, cost delta vs baseline.
3) Failure mode demo (45s): show automatic fallback to cheaper variant and traffic routing.
4) Pilot plan snippet (30s): 90-minute onramp, sample prompts, success metrics.

Speaker note: keep the live demo narrowly scoped: only show one model variant and the dashboard; avoid deep infra configs.

Slide 5 — 90-minute pilot playbook (step-by-step):
- Pre-meeting: ask for 5 representative prompts, current p95 numbers, and a contact with infra access.
- 0–20m: architecture alignment + goal setting (SLOs, cost target).
- 20–60m: run sample prompts through Redwood hosted trial or on-demo VPC; capture token breakdown and latency buckets.
- 60–85m: show results, iterate on batching/caching toggles (we change settings live).
- 85–90m: agree next steps and success criteria for a limited pilot (week-long or reserved capacity trial).

Slide 6 — Quick objection scripts (concise responses):
- "Can we match latency in our region?" → "We can pin the runtime to a region and run a short regional latency sweep during the 90-minute trial; we also support canary routing to your cluster."
- "What about data residency?" → "Private deployments and VPC options with customer KMS are standard; we can kick off a compliance checklist in parallel to the tech pilot."
- "Will results generalize?" → "We measure on your real prompt set and include a small prompt holdout to validate generalization during the pilot."

Slide 7 — Cost vs latency one-liners (for quick throwaway slides):
- "Low cost, variable latency" → hosted standard variants.
- "Predictable latency, reserved cost" → Dedicated pools + reserved capacity.
- "Data control + on-prem security" → Private deployment.

Slide 8 — Competitive differentiators to call out (short bullets):
- Unified API across hosted/dedicated/private — demo the same SDK call.
- Token-level cost visibility — show example screenshot.
- Aggressive KV/prefix caching and auto-batching suggestions — saves tokens without re-engineering prompts.
- Built-in fallback and canary policies — maintain availability during patches.

Slide 9 — Rapid qualification checklist (yes/no):
- Do you have a set of repeatable prompts or templates?
- Is p95 latency or cost variance a blocking metric for your product?
- Can you allocate a 90-minute session with an infra contact?
If 2+ yes → propose a 90-minute pilot.

Slide 10 — Demo artifacts to attach (what to send post-call):
- Export: 90-minute pilot runbook (single-page).
- Attach: sample dashboard PDF with token breakdown.
- Next: pilot success criteria template (metrics & acceptance).
- People: contact list (SE, Solutions Eng, SRE onboarding lead).

Slide 11 — Handy micro-email templates (subject + 1 sentence):
- Subject: "90‑minute pilot: validate latency & cost for LLM serving"
- Body: "Hi <name>, can we run a 90‑minute pilot to measure p95 and per-token cost on your 5 sample prompts? I can set up everything and walk through results in the same session."

Slide 12 — Risk & escalation quick map:
- Risk: pilot shows degraded accuracy with quantized models → Escalation: roll to higher-precision variant and schedule model-eval with applied-ml team.
- Risk: infra not provisioned → Escalation: run hosted trial with masked inputs and follow up for VPC option.

Slide 13 — Measurable success metrics (pilot evaluation):
- Primary: delta in p95 latency and per-token cost vs baseline (both percent and absolute).
- Secondary: change in token usage after caching/batching toggles; correctness drift on holdout prompts.

Slide 14 — Open questions & internal TODO (notes to SEs):
- Get sample prompts in least-privilege form (redact PII) — owner: SE assigned.
- Confirm regional endpoint availability for buyer (APAC/EU).
- Prepare a short script to toggle batching and quantization presets during demo.

Slide 15 — Quick links (internal):
- Pilot runbook (confluence:INF-2719)
- Reserved capacity terms (JIRA:PLAT-982)
- Demo repo (github: atlas-demo PR #14)

—— speaker notes / rough edits:
- This deck is intentionally terse: it's an "arsenal" — copyable one-liners, 90-minute plan, and attachment list.
- Keep it lightweight for Slack shares—one slide can be copy-pasted into a message thread.
- Follow up action: iterate after 5 pilots and fold common objections into the playbook (owner: Maya).

Unresolved draft items:
- Add a mini-case with anonymized numbers showing a 20% cost-down / 30% p95 improvement (need permission).
- Make a one-click demo link for hosted trial (engineering spike: demo-hooks epic).
